bib.title: PlanRAG: A Plan-then-Retrieval Augmented Generation for Generative Large Language Models as Decision Makers
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v1, 18 Jun 2024); the PDF names no venue

read.skipped: reference list and Appendix A (data collection, prompts A.6, re-planning cases A.8) skimmed

question: Can an LLM make a best decision over a large database when it must first plan which analysis to run, and does planning before retrieving beat plain iterative RAG?
hypothesis: Iterative RAG does not plan which analysis the decision needs; adding an explicit plan step and a re-plan step to a ReAct-style loop improves decisions.
contributions: Decision QA: answer the best decision given a question, business rules and a database too large for the prompt

DQA benchmark: 301 question and database pairs (200 Locating, 101 Building) from Europa Universalis IV and Victoria 3, each in relational and graph form, with a simulator that records the ground-truth best decision
PlanRAG: plan, retrieve and answer, re-plan, in one LM prompted with Plan and Re-plan instructions added to ReAct

method.summary: The LM gets question Q, schema S and business rules R and writes a plan of data analyses; it then issues SQL (MySQL) or Cypher (Neo4j) queries through LangChain, reads results, and either retrieves again, re-plans, or answers. Compared with single-turn RAG, iterative RAG (ReAct) and PlanRAG without re-planning.

datasets.name: DQA
datasets.size: 301 pairs: Locating 200, Building 101; 602 databases (RDB and GDB); Locating averages 2038.8 rows per RDB table, Building 579.0
datasets.source: extracted from game data, Paradox Interactive games
datasets.preprocessing: simulator records the result of each decision to annotate the best one

inference.prompting: zero-shot, ReAct with Plan and Re-plan instructions
inference.retrieval: SQL on MySQL, Cypher on Neo4j

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: answer semantically identical to the simulator's best decision

eval.protocol: zero-shot, single run, accuracy averaged over RDB and GDB

results.claim: PlanRAG-LM scores 64.3% (Locating) and 45.0% (Building) against 48.5% and 37.6% for IterRAG-LM and 30.5% and 2.5% for SingleRAG-LM; the abstract's 15.8% and 7.4% are percentage-point gaps.
results.setup: GPT-4, temperature 0, zero-shot, single run, mean over RDB and GDB
results.note: 64.3-48.5 = 15.8 points; 45.0-37.6 = 7.4 points; the abstract writes them as percent

results.claim: Removing re-planning drops PlanRAG-LM to 53.5% (Locating) and 44.1% (Building).
SingleRAG-LM retrieved nothing from the database in over 60% of Locating and 95% of Building questions, because the query needed is too complex to write in one turn.
results.quote: failed to retrieve any results from the database in over 60% of Locating and 95% of Building questions

results.claim: Missed data analysis (a critical value never queried) is 1.3% (Locating) and 21.8% (Building) for PlanRAG-LM against 3.3% and 33.2% for IterRAG-LM.
results.setup: criteria values IV and TP_total (Locating), CO and PD (Building)

results.claim: PlanRAG-LM re-plans on 24 of 400 Locating runs (6%) and 77 of 202 Building runs (38%); accuracy falls as the re-plan count rises (0 re-plans 66.8% and 57.6%; 4 or more 0.0% and 13.3%).
results.n: 400 Locating and 202 Building runs (200 and 101 questions times RDB and GDB)

results.claim: Failure analysis: PlanRAG-LM cuts candidate-selection (CAN) and missed-analysis (MIS) errors but has slightly more DEEP errors (misusing retrieved data or equations), which the authors attribute to those cases now reaching the reasoning step.
results.note: read from the figure and text

limits: Benchmark built from two video games, not real business data; a simulator supplies the ground truth.
One reader, GPT-4, zero-shot, single run; no variance reported.
Only SQL and Cypher over RDB and GDB; vector or hybrid stores not tested.
Single LM only; multi-LM planner/executor split not tested.
Building plans remain hard: 38% of Building runs re-plan and accuracy is 45.0%.
Accuracy figures are means of RDB and GDB; RDB and GDB differ (Table 5).
